text: Working with APIs is an important skill for modern developers. An API allows two programs to communicate with each other. To get data, your application sends HTTP requests to a server, and the server usually responds with JSON, a simple and readable data format. However, you must authenticate first, which means proving your identity with a key or token. Most APIs also have rate limits, so you can only send a certain number of requests per minute. Finally, always add error handling to your code, because networks fail and servers return errors. Good error handling keeps your application stable and gives users a better experience.
